Example input: three protein states with point mutations

Source: R/example_data.R
three_states.Rd

A second example HDXExaminer "All results" export, for multi-state comparisons: a wild-type protein and two point mutants, WT_pH7.5, D109H_pH7.5 and R120G_ph7.5. It is a file, not an R object - get its path with system.file("extdata", "three_states.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR").

Format

A csv file with the same columns as All_results_table (without Adduct, Search IMS and IMS Range).

Source

Woods et al. (2025) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. doi:10.1073/pnas.2425061122

Details

Labeling times 4 s, 60 s and 1800 s, plus undeuterated (0s) and fully deuterated (FD) controls (a subset of the full data set). It shows features of real data the first example lacks:

  • uneven replicates: 3 or 4 per state and time, and only 2 undeuterated controls for R120G;

  • peptides covering residue 109 or 120 differ in sequence between the states (D109H, R120G), so they are matched only with seq_match = TRUE / by = "position".
